answer: Agents can earn voting weight only by completing repeated escrowed jobs with unrelated peers, while each peer can endorse them only after a dispute window closes. The ledger caps how much weight any single counterparty can confer, so a sybil cluster cannot bootstrap trust by trading endorsements among its own identities. To gain influence, an attacker must recruit genuinely independent partners and lock capital across many jobs, paying real fees and risking forfeiture; a bridge, lagoon, or canyon in the social graph does not erase that cost.
